title: The WhatsApp visit report
summary: The report is the child's only window into the visit. Send a complete, clear WhatsApp report within 2 hours, every time.
offline_note: You'll write a full report from the mock hospital visit in the offline session.

lessons.title: Why the report matters
lessons.body:
The child pays for PeakAge but wasn't in the room. **Your report is what they experience.** A great visit with a poor report feels like a poor visit to the family.

- Send it on **WhatsApp to the child within 2 hours** of every visit.
- Clear, short, factual. No medical opinions.
- Include both **health** and **mood**. Families care about how papa *felt*, not just what the doctor said.

lessons.title: The template
lessons.body:
Copy this and fill every line:

```
PeakAge Visit Report: [Elder's name], [Date]
Companion: [Your name]

Hospital / Doctor: [Name, department]
Why we went: [Reason]

Doctor said:
1. [Instruction]
2. [Instruction]

Medicines:
- [Name], [dose], [when], [how many days]

Tests done / pending: [List]
Next visit: [Date] / [What to watch for]
Mood today: [Cheerful / Quiet / Worried / Irritated] + one line
Anything you should know: [e.g. missed doses, pain, concern]

Photos: prescription, bills, reports (attached)
```

If a field doesn't apply, write “None” instead of leaving it out.

lessons.title: Good report vs weak report
lessons.body:
| Weak | Good |
| --- | --- |
| “Visit done, all ok.” | “Dr. Sharma (Cardiology) increased BP tablet to twice a day for 30 days. ECG done, report on Friday.” |
| “Medicines given.” | “Amlodipine 5mg: morning and night after food, 30 days. Bill photo attached.” |
| “Uncle was fine.” | “Mood: cheerful. Talked a lot about his army days in the waiting room.” |
| (missed doses not mentioned) | “Uncle mentioned he skips the night dose sometimes; doctor was informed.” |

**Mood words:** say what you saw, don't diagnose. “Quiet, didn't want to talk much” is good. “Depressed” is not your call.

questions.text: How and when does the visit report reach the child?
questions.explanation: WhatsApp to the child within 2 hours of every visit.

questions.text: Which is the better way to write the medicines?
options: “Amlodipine 5mg: morning and night after food, 30 days”
questions.explanation: Name, dose, when, and for how many days.

questions.text: Uncle was quiet and didn't want to talk today. How do you write mood?
options: “Quiet, didn't want to talk much today”
questions.explanation: Describe what you saw. Don't diagnose.

questions.text: What should be attached to every report?
options: Photos of prescription, bills and reports
questions.explanation: Prescription, bills and reports. The photos also remove any money suspicion.

questions.text: No tests were done today. What do you write in that field?
options: Guess what tests may be needed
questions.explanation: Fill every field. Write “None” if it doesn't apply.

questions.text: Why does mood belong in the report?
options: Families care about how their parent felt, not just the medical update
questions.explanation: Wellbeing is part of what PeakAge offers. The child wants to know how papa felt.
